name_note: Many catalog genomes GTDB assigns to this species carry the NCBI name Akkermansia muciniphila, reflecting the recent separation of Akkermansia massiliensis from that species.

sentences.text: Akkermansia massiliensis is a recently described species of the genus Akkermansia, which belongs to the phylum Verrucomicrobiota and whose best-studied member is the human gut commensal Akkermansia muciniphila.

A review reports that Akkermansia massiliensis has emerged as the second most prevalent Akkermansia species in the human gut, and notes indications that more than one Akkermansia phylotype can co-exist in a subject.

A strain of Akkermansia massiliensis isolated from the faeces of a healthy human donor was reported to be tolerant to bile, to show no aspects of virulence, and to engraft the rat gastrointestinal tract.

A genome-wide association comparison reported a coincident association of multiple sclerosis with Akkermansia massiliensis at the FcRL3 gene, supporting that lower abundance may contribute to predisposition.
